utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not correct. Unfortunately not. Drewienkiewicz's intention was to prevent me from going to Racak to conduct that on-site investigation at all. He wasn't concerned with my safety. He was concerned with me going to Racak and conducting that on-site investigation. He knows why. He was so upset after I told him I was to go to Racak that he insulted me and left, and he was very imposing throughout. He spoke in a raised tone of voice, he kept saying, you can't go there, there are villagers, armed villagers. He made a scene and stormed out.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Ma'am, yesterday you testified that the bodies you saw in the mosque had shoes which looked like military boots. Some had dark grey, others had navy blue military trousers, and they had military belts on those trouser. This is at T-12976. Now, there has been evidence in this case from General Drewienkiewicz who viewed the bodies on the 16th in the gully. And he said that the bodies were in fact, in civilian clothes. Now, are you saying that the bodies you saw in the mosque were not in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying only what I saw, and I entered that in my report. It corresponds to the footage. The bodies I saw in the mosque, the 40 of them, were in the items of clothing as I described. What bodies Drewienkiewicz saw is something I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, you also testified yesterday that Dr. Dobricanin said that on one or two bodies there was damage to the head, injuries to the head where the forensic experts said these had been caused by birds or animals because the corpses had lain outdoors for awhile. That's at T-12976. There's also been evidence from witnesses in this case, including General Drewienkiewicz, that he saw one man who was decapitated and many others who had been shot in the head. Did you observe that when you viewed the bodies?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bodies I saw in the mosque, the 40 of them, contained no such corpses as described by Drewienkiewicz. Dr. Dobricanin is a forensic expert. What he said on the spot and what I repeated was video recorded. You can hear him speaking, examining the bodies, saying these injuries to the head were caused by animals or birds since the corpses had lain outdoors. Among the 40, there was not a corpse who had been decapitated, as Drewienkiewicz would have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, you also testified yesterday that the conclusion was that the cause of death of all these bodies were injuries they sustained from fire-arms, hand-held weapons, and that they had been shot at from a distance. Now, we have evidence that General Drewienkiewicz and other internationals saw the bodies or the bodies they viewed appeared to have been shot in the head at close range. Do you agree or disagree with that observation?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I was not able to observe the same thing Mr. Drewienkiewicz did. We have the conclusions of the commission in written form. The forensic experts stated their opinions. I merely read out one of their sentences, one of their conclusions. The 40 bodies found in the mosque which they carried autopsies of is what we had. Whether there were any other casualties, I don't know. I know of no such cases described by Mr. Drewienkiewicz. I only know that there was a discrepancy between the number of bodies found in the mosque and the number of bodies in the schedule of the indictment against Mr. Milosevic. With the prosecutors we were able to --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... yesterday and I believe you answered my question. Do you agree or disagree with that observation? I don't, I was not able to observe the same thing Mr. Drewienkiewicz did.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'd like to call up a video, and this is the video that I mentioned early on, Your Honours. And Mr. Djordjevic had requested some provenance information on the video. And what we have is that it is an edited version of a video that we obtained from a human rights verifier of the OSCE, someone called M. Pedersen. And the date of the video is the 16th of January, 1999. When the video starts there will also be further information provided about its provenance as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are we to have sound?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, we are, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I think we need to stop what is happening and go back to the beginning and find the sound.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we seem to be having a problem with the sound system. I wonder if I could provide the information verbally and we could return to the speaking portion of the video. The rest of the video is just visual, and it's not necessary to have sound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Defence is opposed to this way of establishing the authenticity of the document especially as such footage, and we had a chance to see it, contains sequences that differ greatly in quality especially with regard to resolution and pixels as part of it are high quality, parts of it are low quality. So the Defence is inclined to believe that this is -- was produced in ill faith. We are not saying that the Prosecution did it, but whoever made the recording should probably also testify to it. And we are also inclined to submit that this should be inspected by an expert to establish the authenticity of this footage, and it's a very long recording. I believe the overall length is about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that the case, Ms. Gopalan?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: In relation to length, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: The total video is about 30 minutes, but I had selected some clips to show to the witness, so in terms of the duration of what we would be viewing in the courtroom will just be a few minutes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, have you made progress with the sound connections?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Doesn't appear to be the case, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think for practicality and to move along conscious of what Mr. Djordjevic has said, we should allow the clips that you wish to put to the witness to be played and to hear the witness's comments, but the question of whether the video or the clips will be accepted as genuine and reliable will be a question that will remain alive and subject to some verification or evidence of another sort. So we will certainly not receive it as an exhibit at the moment. It will need to be marked if it's played, but we will allow the witness to comment on it because that is the significance for the moment of what you intend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If we play the extracted clips that you wish.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, we can see from this video-clip on the screen that this is a person who has been decapitated; correct? Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And now.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, you would agree that this is a head wound?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And does this appear to have been caused by birds or animals?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not an expert to comment such things.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, does this appear to be military clothing to you?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know something, let us get something straight here. The bodies that I found at Racak, those bodies were in the mosque. These are not the same bodies that we saw here. I don't know about these bodies. These two bodies, well, it's clear what happened to them. We saw what they were like, but I didn't find them in Racak. I went around the whole village, but I didn't see these bodies anywhere. I really cannot comment. Was this footage made by an authorised person --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: You remember seeing precisely which bodies you saw? And you are sure that you didn't see these bodies?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not these. And they didn't wear such clothing. I told you what kind of bodies I saw, and there is also video footage where you can see how each body was dressed and what kind of clothes. I believe you saw the pictures and images that we submitted as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And this is another body that appears to have suffered a head wound; correct?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I cannot comment.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: You see that --

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they had been --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: You don't think this looks like a head wound, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can think what I want. I can see something red here, but I haven't seen the body directly. I should have -- that's necessary for me to describe it. This might be red dye, but this also could be blood. The bodies that you are showing me are bodies that I didn't see in Racak. They weren't in the mosque where I saw and identified 40 bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, these bodies here, ma'am, they are not in military clothing, are they? We'll have a look at that again.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can tell, they are wearing civilian clothes of lively colours. Some have dark trousers, but I can't really make out what kind of clothes those are. This is an image that I think I first saw on television when it was published by Walker. If Walker had wanted to co-operate with us, I should have gone to this spot as an investigating judge and established the facts with Walker rather than Walker going there alone. He wasn't authorised to conduct on-site investigations and show footage on TV and draw premature conclusions. I don't know where Walker found them. He is the only one who knows.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. Your Honours, I'll ask that this video is marked for identification, and I will also note that this video is referred to in the statement of General Drewienkiewicz which is in evidence before this Tribunal or this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll, at the moment only be marked for identification, Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1575 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Ma'am, yesterday you testified about the 40 bodies that you've talked about, the 40 bodies in the mosque, and you said Dr. Dobricanin inspected each body visually and immediately stated out loud that there was no trace of any slaughter on those bodies. So based on a visual inspection of 40 bodies in the room, the forensic expert was able to declare that there hadn't been any slaughter?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct what you are saying. He directly examined each body visually and he only commented by saying, I cannot see traces of massacre on these bodies. He didn't use the word "slaughter," nor did I relate his words in that way. He visually expected each body individually and stated that there are no traces to the effect that they were massacred, and later on they were autopsied to establish the cause of death of each individual body.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, you then made a statement, a public statement that these bodies hadn't been massacred; correct?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depends when I said it. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: On the 20th of January, 1999.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To who did I say that?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Let's call up 65 ter 6071, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, we see the article on the screen. Do you see the article head "They Were Not Massacred"?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the headline, but I cannot read the article proper because it's illegible.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could we zoom in, please. It's the small box at the bottom, on the bottom right-hand --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see it, now it's better.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Would you like it bigger? Are you able to read it?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, the English says: "Danica Marinkovic said: 'The terrorist' corpses have not been massacred, as the more than biased head of Kosovo Verification Mission KVM William Walker has claimed." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, well, you have read out only a part of the article, but if you read it all, then the context of my statement is different.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Do you agree, though, that -- or was that your view at the time that the terrorist corpses had not been massacred?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't my view. I had a direct look at the bodies that we found in the mosque and Dobricanin as an expert stated his opinion that there were no traces to that effect. But, of course, I added that the cause of death would be established by an autopsy, so it isn't my view, or my opinion, or my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: So at this stage the autopsies hadn't been completed yet; correct?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 19th, the autopsies started. On two or three bodies the autopsy had already been performed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And you hadn't been able to locate the pit or the gullies where the bodies had been found, the location that Walker had indicated in the broadcast; correct?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. We were unable to find the location or the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And you didn't interview any survivors, did you?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When, on the day when I conducted the on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because we didn't meet anyone in the village. The village was empty. And I had no right to speak to them. I could only take the personal information of anyone who was an eye-witness, but we didn't find anybody in the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And yet you made this statement or you held the view that there hadn't been a massacre. Now, does that strike you as an objective investigation, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, Madam Prosecutor, Walker gave a statement that the bodies had been massacred and he had no evidence to support that or he didn't conduct an on-site investigation. And when I said that he didn't say the truth, I wanted to express that there was a different opinion and that the forensic medicine expert already had stated that there had been no massacre. So I don't see that what I say is all that bad.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: My apologies. Now, the forensic expert that we have seen, that was based on his visual examination, and we are not talking about Walker at the moment, ma'am. We are talking about the investigation you conducted. And I put to you, ma'am, that you did not conduct an objective investigation and the purpose of your investigation was to clear the name of the MUP. Do you agree or disagree?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot claim that because you don't know what I did. And secondly, I say that Walker had no right to go to the site without the judicial bodies present. And he had no right to say that there had been a massacre before the facts are established. Because it serves no one, not you, not me. And I was an investigating judge who merely conducted an investigative activity, an investigative measure, not an entire investigation. It was merely an on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. Your Honours, I believe it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's over time. We will resume at five minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, while the witness is being brought in I am reminded that I did not tender the last newspaper Article, 06071 and I'd like to have that admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P1576, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And the sound issue with the video has been resolved as well, Your Honours, so I'll play the beginning of the video which provides information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you expect to be long now with the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: My estimate would be another half-hour or so, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I wonder whether we might finish tonight.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'm hopeful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You are hopeful you will finish but Mr. Djordjevic may need some time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Ma'am, the bodies that you saw in the mosque on the 18th, now, these were the bodies that had been killed in Racak on the 15th; correct?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what, I cannot assert with any certainty that these were the bodies. I found them in Racak and I suppose they had been killed on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Let's move on to the video that we were viewing just before.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: If I could call that up, it's P1575.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, the video that has just been played, the information provided states that this was a video that was taken in Racak on the 16th. Are you aware that the KVM went to Racak on that date; correct?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day in the evening, you could see it on TV. I can see this footage here as well. However, this was done by unauthorised staff who entered Racak without any state institution representatives.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am. And as the video is played --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: If we could have a look at it, it's just a short clip.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, I represent to you that this is what was seen by the KVM on the 16th. These were the bodies that were seen by William Walker on that day. Ma'am, if you had seen what the KVM saw on the 16th, what we are just viewing now, would you have said that a massacre had occurred?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only tell you that I'm not an expert to ascertain that. Neither was Walker. Had we found these bodies, we would have carried out autopsies in order to establish the cause of death.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Ma'am, we went through a newspaper report and based on your testimony yesterday as well where you declared that a massacre hadn't occurred even before you conducted an autopsy; correct?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not, Madam Prosecutor. I have said it a number of times, the bodies of those whom we found in Racak were not the same as the bodies shown to me now. As an investigating judge, I can also put the question of about whether these people were actually killed there on the spot or were they brought from somewhere else. There is a degree of suspicion, of course, because Walker did so without any representatives of state institutions. Had we done this jointly, we would have been able to provide a joint conclusion. As for what I could see in Racak in the mosque, the 40 bodies there, not a single body had any traces of slaughter. Speaking from my experience, I can say that, and there was also a forensic expert there who was the person authorised to provide an opinion on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. Is this professor Dobricanin that you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was there throughout the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender this clip into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll leave that question for the moment. In view of what has been raised by Mr. Djordjevic, we'll consider that at a later time. We are not dealing with that question now, Mr. Djordjevic, we are leaving it until a later time. Are you moving on, Ms. --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I am, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, you gave a statement to this Tribunal in 2002; correct? We can call it up for you to have a look at it. It's 06082.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean the statement I gave to an investigator of the Prosecution, I think it was in 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: That's right, ma'am. It's 06082. Now, that was about three and a half years after the Racak incident; correct?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I have the statement placed on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: It's being called up, ma'am, we have asked for it.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: So the statement that you gave in 2002, you seem to remember it, and you say that was about three and a half years after events in Kosovo; correct?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 2002, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, did you have an accurate memory of the events in Kosovo in 2002?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I see that the statement is not up yet.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 2002 I was no longer in Kosovo and Metohija, therefore, I cannot tell you exactly what was taking place there. I'm not even sure what you are interested in precisely. If I have any knowledge of it, I can share it with you. But I wasn't in Kosovo any longer. I was interviewed by a Hague investigator in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, we have the statement on the screen, ma'am, and we see that you have signed this statement. I represent to you that you have signed every page of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And if we could go to the end both in the B/C/S and the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: You have certified the statement as being accurate.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I please see the contents. I can only see the front page.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Do you see the final page, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And your certification that this statement is accurate?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And were you accurate and truthful in the statement, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: You testified before this Tribunal in the Milosevic case; right?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And when you testified there, you took an oath to tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And that was in 2005, so about six years after the events in Kosovo; right?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And did you do your best to give an accurate and complete picture or to provide accurate and complete information to the Court in the Milosevic case?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Ma'am, in your 2002 statement and in your Milosevic testimony, you gave evidence about the Racak investigation; right?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And you've already said that you testified correctly and truthfully, and you also testified about events on the 18th of January in Racak; right?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could I call up 65 ter 3115, which is this witness's Milosevic testimony. Page 107. Could we go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, it says here: "On the 18th, in addition to our team and OSCE representatives, there were many representatives of foreign and local media." Now, ma'am, you are being examined by Mr. Milosevic here, and this is in relation to events in Racak. So you say: "On the 18th, in addition to our team and OSCE representatives, there were many representatives of foreign and local media." "Q. You mentioned that already. Was there anyone else? "A. I don't know who you mean. I can't think of anyone at the moment. "Q. I don't mean anyone in particular. I'm just asking." Now, you didn't mention General Djordjevic being in Racak on the 18th, did you?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, I wasn't asked about him at the time. Regarding the 18th and the presence of media representatives, that is correct, but they were present on the spot when we entered Racak.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: So you didn't mention General Djordjevic being in Racak on the 18th because you weren't asked about him at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could we have a look at your statement again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Djordjevic was not in Racak. I never said so.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, you didn't mention General Djordjevic being in the Stimlje police station on the 18th, did you, in the Milosevic case?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't, that is correct. No one asked me about it, and I didn't find it necessary to mention. I didn't even mention Mitic being there. I didn't mention anyone in particular. I didn't mention the chief Janicijevic either.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now if we could have a look at your statement again.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And that is 06082. And if we go to page 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'll read out the paragraph for you.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I can't see the heading of this. What is this? It says statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am, this is your statement that we just saw shortly, the one that you provided to the Tribunal in 2002. And in the English, I'm looking at the paragraph on page 12 that begins with: "On the 18th of January..." and in the B/C/S, that's on page 9.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I can't see a paragraph starting with the 18th.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: It's at the bottom of the page currently on the screen, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, now I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And we'll move it shortly to the next paragraph, to the next page so you are able to read it in full. Now, let me read this paragraph. It says: "On 18th January, 1999, I travelled from Pristina to Stimlje police station with the Prosecutor Dragomir Zivic and Professor Dobricanin. I did not go to any other police station other than Stimlje. There we met inspector Srecko Dabetic --"

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This isn't what the translation says. The sentence starts "there we met," that is, the last sentence you read out is missing from the translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: We can move on to the next page, please, of the B/C/S and stay on the same page of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Do you see it there now?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the top it starts "there to collect evidence at the site."

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'll follow on with the English which reads: "There we met inspector Srecko Dabetic and Sasa LNU, crime technician from SUP Urosevac. (These are the names that I could not remember yesterday). There was another crime technician, Mica LNU, who was there to video record the on-site evidence. I asked the duty policeman what the situation was like during the night, if there had been any shooting throughout the night and the morning, and he said it had been peaceful. The police did not tell me that the mosque was secured and under police security or how many bodies were in there. With this information of no provocation, I decided that we would enter Racak at about noon to commence the investigation." Now, ma'am, in this statement you provide great detail on who was in the Stimlje police station on the 18th. You mention the Prosecutor, you mention a professor, you mention an inspector, and you mention two crime technicians. And you are telling us now that you did not mention that the chief of the RJB, Mr. Djordjevic, was also there?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know something, let's clarify this. What I said here in the statement where I mention the names of those present, this refers to the members of the on-site investigation team because Dabetic is an inspector of general crime of the Urosevac SUP. He is one of the members of the on-site investigation team. The other persons are crime technicians also, members of the on-site investigation team, and they are mentioned in my on-site investigation report as being with me all the time. General Djordjevic was not a team member, nor did he have any authority with regard to the on-site investigation. He came to speak to his colleagues, to the chief of the secretariat, and check whether the situation on the ground was peaceful for the on-site investigation to take place. He came when we were already upstairs where there was also the chief of the secretariat and the chief of the department of the police. He briefly spoke to his colleagues, inquired about the situation in the field and we got up. General Djordjevic didn't interfere with the work nor was it necessary for me to mention him in the on-site investigation report because he wasn't a team member or couldn't be present in any capacity. And nor did anybody ask me about him until my examination here began. But these people here who are team members, they were present. I said the truth. Take a look at my report and you will see that the same persons are mentioned in the on-site investigation report.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: So, ma'am, in a statement you gave to this Tribunal and in previous testimony to this Tribunal, what events in relation to Racak were discussed, you simply failed to mention that the chief of the RJB was present at the Stimlje police station on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, I didn't fail to mention that. I considered it as a piece of non-essential information. It didn't occur to me that it would matter to this Court that I mention General Djordjevic. But I have said the truth in every statement I have given, but nobody has asked me about him until now.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Ma'am, given that the conflict in Racak was a high-profile case, high-profile incident, it was in the media, and it was a conflict involving the police, you considered it a non-essential piece of information to say that the head of the RJB was in the Stimlje police station on the 18th of January?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, he is not the only one I didn't mention. I didn't mention the chief of the secretariat or the chief of the department of the police, and I don't think that is essential information because the incident that happened in Racak was in the morning hours of the 15th, and I went to the on-site investigation from the 15th to the 18th and I set out to go there every morning on those days.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: So, ma'am, until yesterday you have never told this Tribunal that General Djordjevic came to the Stimlje police station on the 18th of January, have you?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't. Nobody asked me. I didn't consider that essential. And that applies not only to him but to other persons as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender the Milosevic testimony and the statement into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You mean the whole of the Milosevic testimony?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Perhaps just the portion that I showed to the witness, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What pages were they?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Pages 107 to 108, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received. The statement will also be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P1577 and P1578, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, you said that the reason you hadn't told this Tribunal about General Djordjevic's presence in the Stimlje police station was because "nobody asked me." Now, ma'am, during your testimony yesterday no one asked you either. In fact, you just volunteered this information, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned it because I knew it was important because I prepared for my testimony by the Defence, and I reviewed the evidence and the statements in this trial.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, did you also mention it because you are aware that this is a contested issue in this case?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know it was contested, but during the proofing with the Defence counsel about the question to be asked, to be -- this arose as an issue in that it's important to mention, and that's why I reckoned I should mention it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Gopalan. Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I have some problem with this microphone. Now, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I believe we will be able to conclude this witness's testimony today and that is why I ask you, Ms. Marinkovic, to provide brief answers to my questions. I tried to shed light on as many details as possible in my direct examination about the situation in Kosovo and Metohija and about the job of an investigating judge. Concerning the fact that my learned friend Ms. Gopalan insisted on the injuries sustained by -- or claimed by Mr. Balaj and others, let me ask you, do you have the right to conduct an investigation outside the request to conduct an investigation by the public prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see the interpretation. No, I don't have that right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Secondly, we saw that those injuries were, in fact, light injuries. Since the criminal report was filed by the police or alternatively if the police did so, or sorry, the defence counsel of any of these persons did so, is there the possibility in that the Criminal Code of Serbia or Yugoslavia or rather an incrimination called inflicting light injuries?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the Serbian Criminal Code there is such a criminal offence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: And which court is -- has subject matter jurisdiction for light injuries?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see the translation on the monitor. The territorial jurisdiction and the subject matter jurisdiction for light bodily injuries are with the municipal court.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And even if a criminal report had been filed, were you in a position to conduct an examination into that as an investigating judge of the district court?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My second question, we heard hearsay incriminations that you are a judge who favours the police. Please explain to this court whether you as an investigating judge at the time acted upon the request of the police or upon the request of the district public prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As investigating judge, I always acted upon the request of the district public prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Did the police have any authority to manage the proceedings and have such a request of you?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Did any government body have such authority?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: My following question has to do with another question of my learned friend Ms. Gopalan. Is it required for you to be the only authorised person, if you run an investigation, to grant permission to forward the accused person to be visited, or can that be done by one of your colleagues in your absence?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in my absence, another colleague can do that. And since there were many cases and many accused persons, there was a court clerk who was in the position to give such permits to lawyers and family members, so that this administrative job was done by a clerk rather than a judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now this is clear also. Ms. Marinkovic, or Judge Marinkovic, please answer me, when you said that Mr. Walker shouldn't have done what he did in the field and we know that my learned friend says that that footage was produced during an investigation of their own, is there a problem that amounts to the destruction of evidence, moving bodies about, was that problem raised immediately after you arrived at the site on the 18th? I am not saying the 15th.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, did Mr. Drewienkiewicz mention the existence of the KLA, or rather, of KLA members at the site in Racak at all? Did he tell you that KLA members were there?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he said villagers. He said armed villagers. He never mentioned KLA members.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: With no single word about the KLA?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: But we have very little time left so I won't go back to the names, but you say that on the 18th OSCE representatives, or rather the KVM were present too; right?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Did they mention that?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Since the Defence is not currently in the position of that videotape, we have an agreement with the Prosecution to enable the Trial Chamber to play two video-clips upon the request of the Defence. The first clip with regard to that footage, but we will not agree yet to it being admitted as evidence, is from 17 minutes 18 seconds to 17 minutes 31 seconds. Can we see that on our screens, please. Is that possible, Madam Prosecutor? It seems to be possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I indicate to help you, Mr. Djordjevic, that we realise that we may be asking too much of you to finish tonight so that can you have time tomorrow as well, if you need it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To be honest, if I could be given an additional 20 minutes, that would contribute to clarifying many issues, and I don't have 20 minutes today. Of course, I will agree to continue tomorrow, I'm very grateful to the Chamber for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You would like to watch the video now? Play the video now? Tomorrow? It's proposed that we adjourn a few minutes early and continue tomorrow which in fairness seems appropriate. We must ask you to come again tomorrow, I am afraid. We resume at 2.15 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 19th day of March, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.52 p.m.
